title: CI/CD pipeline
oneLiner: A release process that checks a new version before release and puts the previous one back when a check misses. Start a demo run.

live.firstAction: Open the demo page and start a check run. Then send a bad version and watch it put the previous one back.
limits: The free instance sleeps after 15 minutes idle and takes about a minute to wake.
The demo page starts one action at a time; the buttons stay disabled while a run is in flight.
A full gate run takes several minutes and spends the repository's Actions minutes.

shots.alt: Pipeline demo page at rest: three action cards — Run the gates, Ship a bad image and Roll back — beside a Live panel that reports no action running, a recent-runs table, and a footer naming the live and previous deploys.

Pipeline demo page mid-run: the Run the gates card reads running under run 40949046956, and the job list shows image, lint, test (22), migration-gate, typecheck, bundle-size and git-leaks all in progress.

Pipeline demo page rollback: a six-step timeline reading deploy.start, health.ok, smoke.fail, rollback.start, rollback.health.ok and rollback.smoke.ok, with the two deploy ids dep-dbhqqoec6qcc73842uc0 and dep-dbhqq888v5cc7396at9g in the footer.
Pipeline demo page after the bad-image run: the build job reports success, the Trivy job reports a HIGH finding, and the banner names bad-image-trivy while the run finishes red.

invariants.claim: Unauthenticated POST /invoices is rejected with 401; an authenticated request returns 201 with a UUID id
GET /ready reports 503 pending_migrations when a migration is unapplied, and 200 when database and migrations are okay
An unknown invoice id returns 404 not_found with no stack trace in the body

limits: A full run spends the repository's Actions minutes.
The Actions PostgreSQL service is configured separately from local PostgreSQL 16.
Rollback returns one release and is built for expand/contract migrations.
